levels.title: DAX 1 · Clean Syntax & Formatting Basics
levels.concept_capsule: In Power BI, separating intermediate logic with `VAR`/`RETURN` and wrapping output in `COALESCE` prevents `(Blank)` cards and keeps measures easy to audit.
levels.reference_solution:
-- Total net sales measure
Total Sales :=
VAR _TotalAmount = SUM ( Sales[Amount] )
RETURN
    COALESCE ( _TotalAmount, 0 )

keywords_glossary.role: Stores an intermediate expression evaluated once in the current filter context. In production, it simplifies debugging in DAX Studio.
Declares the final expression returned by the measure. In production, it separates calculation steps from final output cleanly.
Returns the first non-BLANK argument. In production, it prevents executive KPI cards from displaying `(Blank)` on empty filters.

formatting_mechanics.indentation: Indent the final expression 4 spaces beneath `RETURN` following DAX Formatter conventions.
formatting_mechanics.line_breaks: Put the measure header `:=` on line 1, each `VAR` on its own line, `RETURN` on its own line, and the output indented below.
formatting_mechanics.punctuation: Add spaces around `:=` and `=`, and pad function parentheses (`SUM ( Table[Col] )`).
formatting_mechanics.documentation_standard: Start the measure with a `-- ` comment describing its business definition.

analogous_example.title: Inventory units measure without BLANK
analogous_example.code:
-- Total available units in inventory
Total Units :=
VAR _TotalQty = SUM ( Inventory[Qty] )
RETURN
    COALESCE ( _TotalQty, 0 )
analogous_example.why_it_works: Combines a `-- ` header, `VAR`/`RETURN`, DAX Formatter spacing, and `COALESCE` on an unrelated inventory table.

levels.title: DAX 2 · Edge Cases & Documentation
levels.concept_capsule: Replacing `/` with `DIVIDE(..., 0)` and caching reused measures in `VAR` prevents `Infinity` visuals and avoids redundant VertiPaq engine scans.
levels.reference_solution:
-- Safe profit margin percentage using DIVIDE
Margin Pct :=
VAR _Sales = [Sales]
VAR _Cost = [Cost]
RETURN
    DIVIDE ( _Sales - _Cost, _Sales, 0 )

remedial_drills.solution_hint: Use `VAR` variables for readability and performance.

keywords_glossary.role: Performs safe division returning the fallback (`0`) when the denominator is zero or `BLANK`. In production, it prevents `Infinity` values in Power BI charts.
Evaluates a reused measure once inside a `VAR`. In production, it cuts query time on multi-million-row fact tables.
Computes the final ratio from the cached variables. In production, it keeps ratio logic transparent during code reviews.

formatting_mechanics.indentation: Keep `VAR` and `RETURN` left-aligned and indent `DIVIDE` by 4 spaces under `RETURN`.
formatting_mechanics.line_breaks: Place one `VAR` per line, followed by `RETURN` and the indented result.
formatting_mechanics.punctuation: Pad `DIVIDE ( a, b, 0 )` parentheses with spaces and put a space after each comma.
formatting_mechanics.documentation_standard: Open with a `-- ` comment stating the KPI ratio and its zero-denominator guard.

analogous_example.title: Safe logistics fulfillment rate
analogous_example.code:
-- Safe shipment fulfillment ratio using DIVIDE
Fulfillment Rate :=
VAR _Ordered = [Orders Placed]
VAR _Shipped = [Orders Shipped]
RETURN
    DIVIDE ( _Shipped, _Ordered, 0 )
analogous_example.why_it_works: Caches both measures in `VAR` and uses `DIVIDE ( ..., 0 )` to guard zero denominators in a logistics domain.
